subtopics.title: A Dry Country by the Numbers

questions.question: South Africa's average annual rainfall compares with the world average as roughly:
options: 465 millimetres against 860 — a little more than half the world's ration
860 millimetres against 465 — nearly double the world average
200 millimetres against 2 500
Equal to the world average

questions.question: The rule governing rainfall across South African space is:
options: Rain increases steadily from east to west
Rain falls evenly across all provinces
Rain decreases from east to west, from over 1 000 millimetres to under 50
Rain falls mainly along the northern border

questions.question: Evaporation matters to the water budget because over most of the interior:
options: It only occurs in summer
The atmosphere could lift more water off an open surface in a year than the sky delivers
It adds moisture to the rivers
It is weaker than in wetter countries

questions.question: The runoff figure worth memorising is that:
options: Half of all rainfall reaches the rivers
No rainfall reaches the rivers in dry years
A quarter of rainfall recharges aquifers
Only about 9 per cent of South Africa's rainfall ever becomes river flow

subtopics.title: Rivers of South Africa — Perennial and Not

questions.question: The Orange, or Gariep, flows through near-desert in its lower course because:
options: It is fed by winter rain in Namaqualand
Local storms sustain it year-round
It carries water gathered far away in the Lesotho highlands across the dry west
It flows underground for most of its length

questions.question: The eastward-flowing rivers such as the Thukela are short and steep yet carry the best flows because:
options: The escarpment stands close to that coast and drains its wettest slopes
They are fed by melting glaciers
The Indian Ocean pushes water inland
They are the country's longest rivers

questions.question: An episodic river, such as the Molopo or Auob:
options: Flows every day of the year
Flows only after occasional heavy storms, and may lie dry for years
Flows only in winter
Never carries water at all

questions.question: Travelling west across South Africa, the river types change in the order:
options: Episodic, perennial, periodic
Periodic, episodic, perennial
Perennial everywhere until the coast
Perennial, then periodic, then episodic — matching the thinning rainfall

questions.question: South Africa has almost no natural freshwater lakes because:
options: Its lakes were all drained for farming
The coastline is too straight for lakes
Natural lakes need glaciers or rivers with spare water, and our warm, dry history supplied neither
Earthquakes destroyed the ancient lakes

questions.question: Sterkfontein Dam's special job in the national system is to:
options: Serve as a strategic reserve, filled by water pumped up from the Thukela and used only in drought
Generate most of the country's electricity
Supply Cape Town directly
Trap silt before it reaches the Vaal Dam

questions.question: Groundwater's two great advantages over surface water are that it:
options: Is always purer and always renewable
Hides from evaporation and waits beneath places that have no rivers
Flows faster and costs nothing to pump
Never runs out and never pollutes

questions.question: Acid water draining from derelict mines is a serious groundwater threat because:
options: It evaporates too quickly to trace
It only affects rivers, never boreholes
It improves the taste of borehole water
Contamination that seeps into an aquifer is close to impossible to remove

questions.question: Gauteng illustrates the mismatch of people and water because it:
options: Sits on a high watershed with no major river, placed there by gold rather than by water
Receives the country's highest rainfall
Lies below sea level
Has more dams than any other province

questions.question: The single largest user of South Africa's water is:
options: Household gardens
Mining
Irrigation agriculture, at roughly 60 per cent of the total
Power stations

questions.question: Alien invasive plants such as wattle, pine and gum reduce water availability because they:
options: Poison the rivers they grow beside
Block dam walls with their roots
Shade the water and stop evaporation
Transpire far more than the indigenous vegetation they displaced, intercepting runoff

questions.question: Non-revenue water refers to:
options: Water reserved by law for river ecosystems
Treated water lost through burst pipes, failed meters and unbilled use — a third or more in many municipalities
Rain that never reaches the rivers
Water exported to neighbouring countries

questions.question: In the rain-tank picture of the country, the weak gutter stands for:
options: South Africa's rainfall running at barely half the world's average
The country's shortage of dam engineers
The high cost of municipal water
The pollution in urban rivers

questions.question: Only about 9 litres of every 100 litres of rain that land on South Africa:
options: Fall on farmland
Evaporate before touching the ground
Reach a river where they can be captured and used
Soak into aquifers

questions.question: The gutter hangs on one side of the roof means:
options: Most dams were built in the wrong provinces
Rain falls generously in the east and hardly at all in the west, far from many of the people
Rain falls only at the coast
The west gets all the summer thunderstorms

subtopics.title: A Road Trip from Wet to Dry

questions.question: Driving west from Durban, the rivers crossed change in the order:
options: Episodic, periodic, perennial
Perennial, episodic, periodic
Perennial, periodic, episodic — the rainfall map drawn in rivers
Periodic, perennial, episodic

questions.question: A perennial river keeps flowing between rains because:
options: Saturated ground keeps seeping water into its channel
Dams release water into it daily
It is fed by ocean tides
Its channel is too deep to dry out

questions.question: The Orange breaks the wet-to-dry pattern of the road trip because:
options: It flows underground through the Karoo
It only flows after storms
It collects winter rain from the west coast
It obeys Lesotho's rainfall, not the desert's — delivering mountain water across the dry west

subtopics.title: The Country That Built Its Own Lakes

questions.question: South Africa's handful of natural lakes includes:
options: The Vaal Dam and Gariep
Fundudzi, the Chrissiesmeer pans and coastal Sibaya
Theewaterskloof and Midmar
Sterkfontein and Jozini

questions.question: The two taxes every South African dam pays are:
options: Floods and droughts
Alien plants and boreholes
Evaporation lifting water off the top while silt fills the dam from the bottom
Pumping costs and municipal rates

questions.question: The first rule of the underground water account is:
options: Withdraw no faster than rain recharges the aquifer, or the water table sinks year by year
Drill boreholes as deep as possible
Pump only in summer
Share one borehole per province

questions.question: Theewaterskloof earned its place in the world's vocabulary because:
options: It is the largest dam in Africa
It generates Cape Town's electricity
It was the first dam built on the Orange
Its near-empty floor in 2018 marked Cape Town's countdown to Day Zero
